effects.journal: The lockers were closed in 2011. Keys were never taken back.

lines: Closed in 2011. Keys not taken back.
Locker 14 has a new padlock in her photo. Someone is still using a dead locker.
The Courier article about Wren links to something from 2006. Read it before you call anyone.

g_2006.text: Open the 2006 archive article linked from the Courier's missing-person story.

effects.journal: Caleb Voss, 17, vanished 18 November 2006 - the week the council voted to flood the last of the old town. Called a runaway. Jonah Hale was the boy he loved.

lines: Caleb Voss. Seventeen. Last seen 18 November 2006.
The same week the council voted five to two to flood the east basin orchard and its frost-relay grid.
Jonah Hale was the boy he loved. The town called it nothing.

options.text: This is {player}. Wren's friend. I know about locker 14.
This is {player}. I was talking to Wren the night she went quiet. I think you were the last person she called.
Jonah. I read about Caleb. I'm sorry.

jo1_caleb.text: Don't put his name in a text.

options.text: Tess. She's scared. So am I.
Does it matter? You never answered any of Wren's messages.

jo2_sharp.text: I answered every one of them. Just not in writing.

jo2.text: Not like this. I'm calling you. Pick up.

script.text: Don't say names. Don't say the locker. Phones in this town have a way of getting read.
You were the one she was going to see that night. She told me. 'Someone who doesn't know anything about this place.'

choice.text: Why do you never write anything down?

script.text: Because twenty years ago the boy I loved wrote things down. In a notebook. And everything he wrote came true for him.
So no. I don't write. I show up at a diner and I sit there so people know someone's watching her. Fat lot of good it did.
She found what I told her not to look for. I gave her one page. One. She worked out the rest herself. She was faster than me.
The locker's Caleb's. Fourteen. The code isn't written anywhere. It's in the grid he cut into the door that summer.
Go at low light. Don't park at the marina. And if you see a dark car with council plates, you turn around.
No. If I'm seen with you, you're finished here. Go alone. You'll know the locker when you see it.
Forty-seven seconds. That's all I got from her that night. I've listened to it a hundred times. Be careful.
Low light. Don't park at the marina. Go.
Don't say his name on a phone. I mean it. Not on a phone. Not to Locke, not to the Courier, not to Mara.

lines: He hung up when you said Caleb's name.
The line stayed dead. He will not text. He will not call back today.
But Wren's note said locker 14. And her photo of the locker door shows a grid cut into the metal. You can still go.

effects.journal: Jonah shut down when I said Caleb's name on the phone. I have to earn that back.

s_marina.title: The marina, 6:10 PM
lines: Low light. You park at the diner and walk the shore path.
The north dock lockers are a row of rust. Fourteen has a new brass padlock - four-digit keypad - and something cut into the door under thirty years of paint.
A grid. Nine by nine. Some squares are cut deeper than the others.

mg_grid1.title: Scratched into locker 14

config.brief: Caleb cut this into locker 14 in 2006. Most squares are already filled. Put 1–9 in every row, column and box. The deeper squares hold the code.

hints: Look for a row or box with only one empty square. That number is forced.
If a digit is missing from a row and only one cell can take it, put it there.
Read the shaded cells top to bottom, left to right - that is the order of the code.

effects.journal: The grid on the locker door solves to a four-digit code.

mg_pad1.title: Brass padlock

config.label: Padlock - 4 digits
config.clue: The deeper-cut squares, read top to bottom.

hints: The code is the four digits you just found in the grid.

effects.journal: Locker 14: a notebook of hand-drawn grids, and a Polaroid of the spillway house.

lines: A school notebook, warped by damp. Page after page of nine-by-nine grids in pencil. Some squares shaded hard enough to dent the paper.
Tucked inside the cover: a Polaroid of the spillway house in daylight, years ago.
And on the inside cover, in a different hand, recent: "W - page 2 is the archive. page 3 is the bell. don't do it in order. - J"

g_notebook.text: Her photo of the locker contents just synced. Compare it with what you found.

effects.journal: Her photo is stamped Wed 12:02 AM. She opened this locker fifteen minutes after her last message to me.

lines: SAM-COTTAGE-WIFI. Eleven days ago. 11:52 PM.
Five minutes after "I'll leave the door open." She came. She stood in your kitchen with her phone in her hand while you waited upstairs, asleep, ten metres away.
She didn't knock. She linked her phone to yours and left.
This was never an accident.
